source_text:
Μηδεὶς πλανάσθω: καὶ τὰ ἐπουράνια καὶ ἡ δόξα τῶν ἀγγέλων καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὁρατοί τε καὶ ἀόρατοι, ἐὰν μὴ πιστεύσωσιν εἰς τὸ αἷμα Χριστοῦ, κἀκείνοις κρίσις ἐστίν: ὁ χωρῶν χωρείτω. τόπος μηδένα φυσιούτω: τὸ γὰρ ὅλον ἐστὶν πίστις καὶ ἀγάπη, ὧν οὐδὲν προκέκριται.
καταμάθετε δὲ τοὺς ἑτεροδοξοῦντας εἰς τὴν χάριν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐλθοῦσαν, πῶς ἐναντίοι εἰσὶν τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ. περὶ ἀγάπης οὐ μέλει αὐτοῖς, οὐ περὶ χήρας, οὐ περὶ ὀρφανοῦ, οὐ περὶ θλιβομένου, οὐ περὶ δεδεμένου ἢ λελυμένου, οὐ περὶ πεινῶντος ἢ διψῶντος.
thought_title: No one should be deceived: judgment awaits even heavenly powers without faith in Christ's blood
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Smyrnaeans against false teachers, saying that even heavenly beings face judgment unless they believe in the blood of Christ, and that no position should make anyone proud.
pass_a_gloss: Let no one be deceived: both the heavenly things and the glory of the angels and the rulers, visible and invisible, if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, for them also there is judgment. Let the one who can receive it receive it. Let a position puff up no one: for the whole is faith and love, than which nothing is preferred. But learn about those who hold different opinions concerning the grace of Jesus Christ that came to us, how contrary they are to the mind of God. About love they have no care, not about a widow, not about an orphan, not about one who is afflicted, not about one who is bound or released, not about one who is hungry or thirsty.

lemmas.gloss: the one who can receive it

choices.why: Neuter plural article with adjective, referring to heavenly realities or beings; kept literal as a substantive

choices.term: οἱ ἄρχοντες ὁρατοί τε καὶ ἀόρατοι
choices.why: Keeps the literal noun 'rulers' and the paired adjectives in their source order

choices.english: for them also there is judgment
choices.why: Crasis of καὶ ἐκείνοις; the dative of possession is rendered literally with 'for them also'

choices.english: Let the one who can receive it receive it
choices.why: The participle and imperative of χωρέω echo Matthew 19:12; rendered with the same verb repeated
rejected: He who is able to accept this, let him accept it
Whoever can accept this should accept it

choices.english: Let a position puff up no one
choices.why: τόπος here means rank or position; φυσιόω is literally 'to puff up', kept for its vividness
rejected: Let no one be puffed up by position
Let place puff up no one

choices.why: The participle means 'thinking differently'; rendered as a substantive participle to keep the verbal force

pass_b_english: Let no one be deceived. Even the heavenly things, the glory of the angels, and the rulers both visible and invisible: if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, judgment awaits them as well. Let the one who can receive this receive it. Let no one be puffed up by position, for the whole matter is faith and love, and nothing is preferred above these.

But take careful note of those who hold different opinions about the grace of Jesus Christ that has come to us, and see how contrary they are to the mind of God. They have no care for love, none for the widow, none for the orphan, none for the afflicted, none for the one who is bound or the one who is free, none for the one who hungers or thirsts.

problems.why: The phrase ὁ χωρῶν χωρείτω is a common proverbial expression, not a citation of Matthew 19:12; no scripture is cited here.
problems.fix: Let the one who can receive it receive it.

edits.old: Let the one who can receive it receive it (Matthew 19:12).
edits.new: Let the one who can receive it receive it.

fixed: Removed the incorrect scripture citation Matthew 19:12; the phrase is a proverbial expression, not a biblical citation.

problems.quote: Let a position puff up no one, for the whole is faith and love
problems.why: 'The whole is faith and love' is telegraphic; 'whole' = 'sum total' or 'complete reality'?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'The entirety [of Christian life] is faith and love.'

edits.old: for the whole is faith and love
edits.new: for the sum of all things is faith and love

problems.quote: the sum of all things is faith and love
problems.why: 'Sum' (Greek: telos or kephalaion?) may mean 'goal,' 'culmination,' or 'summary'; 'sum' is mathematically reductive.
problems.fix: Consider 'the goal of all things' or 'the crown of all things'.

edits.old: for the sum of all things is faith and love
edits.new: for the whole is faith and love

fixed: The English 'the sum of all things' was flagged as reductive; the source says 'the whole' (τὸ γὰρ ὅλον), so I restored the literal 'the whole is faith and love' to match the Greek exactly.

problems.quote: the whole is faith and love, and nothing is preferred above these
problems.why: 'The whole' (to holon) is obscure; does it mean 'the whole matter,' 'the universe,' or 'perfection'?
problems.fix: Add note: 'the whole' = 'the entirety' or 'the sum of perfection.'

edits.old: for the whole is faith and love, and nothing is preferred above these.
edits.new: for the entirety is faith and love, and nothing is preferred above these.

fixed: The English already says what the source says; 'the whole' is a literal rendering of to holon, and the suggested note is interpretive rather than a mistranslation. I changed 'the whole' to 'the entirety' to clarify the meaning without adding a note.

problems.quote: the entirety is faith and love
problems.why: 'Entirety' is obscure; likely 'the whole matter' or 'the sum of everything'.
problems.fix: Revise to 'the sum of everything is faith and love'.

edits.old: for the entirety is faith and love
edits.new: for the sum of everything is faith and love

fixed: The source reads 'τὸ γὰρ ὅλον ἐστὶν πίστις καὶ ἀγάπη' (for the whole is faith and love). 'Entirety' is obscure; 'the sum of everything' better conveys the sense of 'the whole' as the totality of what matters.

problems.quote: the whole is faith and love
problems.why: 'The whole' is cryptic; likely 'the whole matter' or 'the sum of everything'.
problems.fix: 'the whole matter is faith and love'.

edits.old: for the whole is faith and love
edits.new: for the whole matter is faith and love

fixed: The source has 'τὸ γὰρ ὅλον ἐστὶν πίστις καὶ ἀγάπη' (for the whole is faith and love). The English 'the whole' is cryptic; 'the whole matter' clarifies the sense without changing the meaning.

last_rejected.quote: Let a position puff up no one
last_rejected.why: τόπος means 'place/region', not 'position'; 'position' is a modern sense not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: Let no place make anyone proud, for the whole is faith and love.
last_rejected.ruling: τόπος can mean 'position/status' figuratively; LSJ cites this very usage. Within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: none for the one who is bound or the one who is free
last_rejected.why: λελυμένου means 'released' (from prison), not 'free' in a general sense; contrast is prisoner vs. released prisoner.
last_rejected.fix: none for the prisoner or the one who has been released
last_rejected.ruling: λελυμένου means 'released/loosed'; 'free' is a natural rendering of the bound/released contrast.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of judgment, smoothed the awkward phrase about position and the sum of all things, and made the sentence rhythm more natural for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.fix: Clarify: 'The entirety [of Christian life] is faith and love.'

polish.changed: Clarified 'the sum of everything' as 'the goal of everything' to convey the intended sense of culmination, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving all claims and qualifications.

notes.quote: the sum of everything is faith and love
notes.fix: 'the goal of everything' or 'the crown of everything'.

polish.changed: Clarified that the heavenly things, angels, and rulers are all subjects who must believe in Christ's blood or face judgment; smoothed sentence rhythm and made the contrast with false teachers flow naturally for reading aloud.

notes.quote: Even the heavenly things, the glory of the angels, and the rulers both visible and invisible: if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, judgment awaits them too.
notes.why: Angels and rulers 'believe' or are judged? Theological claim compressed.
notes.fix: Explain: even angelic powers are subject to Christ's redemption.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'them' refers to the heavenly things, angels, and rulers; smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, judgment awaits them too
notes.why: 'Them' = angels/heavenly powers? Suggests angels judged for disbelief, unusual doctrine.
notes.fix: Note this is exceptional teaching about angelic need for redemption.
